text:
alex: Flagging an onboarding regression: the JS sample for Edge-targeted apps is getting stuck in auth retry loops after we published the last SDK patch. Works in Node but fails on Vercel Edge.

sophie: quick repro please?

alex: steps: clone sample-app, npm i, vercel dev --listen 3000 --edge. Call /api/chat and open logs. You see repeated 401 -> retry -> timeout.

diego: I dug in. The runtime bundle is resolving the package to the ESM node entry (dist/esm/index.mjs) instead of our dist/edge entry. That ESM entry expects a server-side token refresher and uses node-fetch-ish shims so token refresh fails in the worker.

sophie: our package.json exports currently have conditions: ["import","node","edge","default"] (in that order). Some bundlers pick the first matching condition, others prioritize edge when environment indicates worker. Vercel's resolver appears to prefer import over edge unless the consumer build sets a condition.

alex: sample's esbuild config doesn't set conditions explicitly. We expected Vercel to set the runtime condition automatically. Apparently not.

diego: two problems: (1) resolution order allows non-edge entry in edge runtime, and (2) types for TS users are generic and point to a shared d.ts that includes Node-only overloads. TS consumers end up with types that don't match the runtime behavior which leads to mistaken code paths in app code.

sophie: options: reorder exports so "edge" appears before "import"; add a tiny edge entrypoint that exports only the worker-compatible set; add docs for bundlers to prefer edge conditions; or make runtime entry detect worker environment and delegate.

alex: I'd avoid runtime detection hacks if reorder + docs fix it. Which consumers are affected? Vercel and Cloudflare workers most likely.

diego: also adding a small CI test that runs vercel dev against the sample would catch this earlier. We can add a GH Action job that runs vercel dev in background and hits /api/chat.

sophie: TS fix: publish separate d.ts files and point "types" to a top-level index.d.ts that re-exports a conditional union? TS doesn't support conditional exports, but we can ship types/edge/index.d.ts and types/node/index.d.ts and update README to instruct advanced users to set "typeRoots" or import from the explicit path when targeting edge. Not ideal.

alex: Could we instead keep types simple and mark Node-only overloads as deprecated in comments for the next major, and for now make sure the runtime is correct so types at least match behavior 99% of time.

diego: I'm going to open a patch: reorder exports to ["edge","import","require","default"], add dist/edge/index.mjs trivial shim that throws early on non-worker (so Node can't accidentally import it), and update the sample esbuild config in the repo to set conditions: ["edge"].

sophie: add a small note in the sample README and a checkbox in the onboarding checklist. Also ping support channels with a short bulletin.

ops-bot: Issue created: #4598 "edge resolve picks non-edge entry -> auth retry loop in sample" (priority: P3)

alex: timeline?

diego: PR today for exports + sample patch. CI edge smoke job early next week. If green, release a patch ASAP and update sample.

sophie: I'll follow up on the TS ergonomics after the exports fix lands.

alex: thanks — unblocks onboarding for edge users. :rocket:
